I'm beginning to think I was because of how strongly worded my message was.

The whole group was supposed to attend a party that morning, but Friend1's dad died, so she wasn't going to the party. Then, Friend2, who is 17, had bought alcohol for the party, even though she's underage. When she heard about Friend1's dad, she didn't say anything in the group chat. That seems a bit cold, but maybe she was just in shock or didn't know what to say. Then, Friend2 messaged Friend1 in the group chat asking if she was still going to the party and if not, could she give her any alcohol she had bought. That seems really insensitive, especially on the day Friend1's dad died. I can see why that would upset someone. I, being 17, saw this and thought it was out of order. I messaged Friend2 privately and told her it was a really cunty thing to do on the day her dad died. I called her pathetic and said she should be ashamed of herself. That was pretty strong. Then, Friend2 left the group chat, went to the party, and then came to school on Monday and dropped out. She had said before that she was only in school this year to hang out with us. Friend1 is obviously dealing with family stuff and not into petty friend drama, but she did tell Friend2 to fuck off as well. I talked to Friend1 briefly about it before I messaged Friend2 privately. Now, I'm being blamed by Friend2's friends, who weren't in the group chat, for her leaving school. They say I helped bully her out of school. But then, my strong words led to Friend2 leaving the group chat, going to the party, and dropping out of school. I need to think about whether my actions were appropriate or if they crossed a line into bullying. On one hand, I was standing up for Friend1 and calling out inappropriate behavior. On the other hand, my strong language and direct confrontation might have contributed to Friend2 feeling attacked or isolated, leading to her dropping out. I also need to consider the impact of my actions on the group dynamic. By confronting Friend2 privately, I might have caused tension that led to her leaving the group chat and, ultimately, dropping out of school. Her friends are now blaming me, which adds to the pressure I'm feeling. Another aspect to consider is the intention behind my actions. I wanted to support Friend1 and address what I saw as hurtful behavior from Friend2. But the way I did it was through strong, confrontational messages, which might have been more harmful than helpful. I also need to think about the broader implications of my actions. Bullying is a serious issue, and if my actions contributed to someone dropping out of school, that's a significant consequence. Additionally, I should reflect on whether there were other ways to address the situation without resorting to strong language. I also need to consider the role of the group in all of this. Friend1 was dealing with her own grief, and the group dynamics might have made it harder for Friend2 to handle the situation. Overall, I think I need to reflect on the balance between standing up for what's right and doing so in a way that doesn't escalate the situation or cause unintended harm.
